extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of journalism, media studies, and racial/minority representation; journalists and newsroom managers interested in coverage equity
extracted.subtask_description: Goodreads book listing and short summary plus community reviews for Don Heider's White News, which analyzes why local TV news undercovers people of color and introduces the concept of 'incognizant racism'. The page is a consumer-facing synopsis and brief reviews rather than a formal guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of local news
rubrics_metrics.description: If the purpose of local news is to cover individual communities and to present issues of interest and concern to local audiences, why are local newscasts so similar in markets around the country?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative implication: local newscasts should reflect the specific concerns and makeup of their communities rather than follow a homogenous formula; assessors should check how well a newscast attends to locally relevant issues and diversity of community interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful coverage of people of color
rubrics_metrics.description: Heider investigates why local television news coverage of people of color does not occur in more meaningful ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether coverage of people of color includes context, voices, and issues that reflect their communities meaningfully (not tokenistic or superficial). Look for frequency, depth, and framing of stories about communities of color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of editorial content ('white' news vs anchors)
rubrics_metrics.description: "White" news (content determined by white managers) being delivered by non-white news anchors, thus giving the appearance of "non-white" news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between who shapes editorial decisions and who appears on screen; evaluate whether diversity in on-air staff corresponds to diversity in editorial control and story selection, not only presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disproportionate negative portrayals of minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Minderheiten überproportional häufig in negativen Kontexten – insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit Kriminalität – erscheinen (minorities appear disproportionately often in negative contexts, especially crime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess story selection and framing for overrepresentation of minorities in crime/negative stories; check balance of positive, neutral, and negative portrayals and whether narratives reinforce stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and address 'incognizant racism'
rubrics_metrics.description: Heider sets forth a new theoretical concept—incognizant racism—as a way of explaining how news workers consistently ignore news in significant portions of the communities they cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should identify subtle, routine practices that produce racial omission or bias (not only overt prejudice) and implement structural changes to surface and correct these blind spots (training, beats, sourcing practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom decision-making, routines, and selection mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides important insights into the newsroom decision-making process and the sociology and structure of newsrooms; critiques how routines, selection mechanisms, and editorial blind spots reproduce stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate organizational routines (assignment practices, sourcing, gatekeeping) that shape coverage; look for institutional causes of biased coverage and for recommended procedural reforms or solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of audience perception effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers how coverage of minorities influences viewers' perceptions of their minority neighbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess not just content but likely audience effects — how framing and frequency of coverage shape public perceptions — and whether outlets take responsibility for mitigating harmful perceptual impacts.
